stem.en: Why do roads in the hills wind round the slopes instead of going straight up?

text.en: A winding road makes the hill lower.
Each part is a gentle ramp, so less force is needed.
A winding road is shorter than a straight one.
Vehicles do less work on a winding road.

explanation.en: A winding road is a long, gentle ramp. For the same rise in height, a longer path means a smaller force is needed to climb. The work done against gravity is the same, mgh, because the height gained is the same; the path is longer, not shorter.

hints.en: Think of the road as an inclined plane.
What happens to the effort when a ramp is longer for the same height?
